question: Two trains are moving in opposite directions at speeds of 50 km/h and 80 km/h. The length of one train is 480 m. The time taken by them to cross each other is 28 seconds. The length (in m) of the other train, correct to 2 decimal places, is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed of trains in opposite directions = 50 + 80 = 130 km/h.

Convert speed to m/s: 130 × (5/18) = 325/9 m/s.

Total distance covered = Speed × Time = (325/9) × 28 = 9100/9 ≈ 1011.11 m.

Length of the second train = Total distance − Length of the first train.

Length of second train = 1011.11 − 480 = 531.11 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 531.11 m.**
